evidence: paper: Y_i = J_g^{\,i} Y \pmod{\mathbb{Z}^2}, \qquad i = i(\ell) = \left\lfloor \log_{T_g} \frac{Q^{-1-h}}{S_*} \right\rfloor.

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both halves are present. Y_i = J_g^i Y is `cover ^ i` applied to the graph: nativeGraph is exactly (cover ^ nativeIndex h n) applied to r^{d_r}v_r + t v_t, again on the universal cover rather than in 𝕋², with the quotient carried by torusEq (cover_pow_torusEq is the statement that J_g^i descends to the torus, so the cover representative determines Y_i mod ℤ²). The index formula is nativeArgument h n = log(Q_n^{-1-h}/n²)/log(T_g), which is log_{T_g}(Q^{-1-h}/S_*) with S_* = ℓ² = n², and nativeIndex is its floor. One convention: Lean takes the natural-number floor ⌊·⌋₊, which clamps to 0 where the paper's integer floor ⌊·⌋ would be negative. The two agree exactly on the range the paper uses, since nativeArgument_nonneg gives 0 ≤ nativeArgument h n for h ≥ 0 and n ≥ 4, and the paper restricts to "Only large ℓ, for which i(ℓ) ≥ 0". The paper's deck-translation characterization of which functions descend to the band torus (translations a with J_g^i a ∈ ℤ²) is not stated as a declaration in this form; the repository instead works with liftedSupport, the set of ℤ²-reindexed copies of a slot at level i.
